items.response: Added: Grace's 68th birthday on Thu 19 Nov 2026. I'll set a reminder for Thu 5 Nov, two weeks ahead, to sort a gift. Action: Create the all-day birthday event, repeat it yearly, and add the 5 Nov gift reminder.

TFSA: you contribute after-tax money, it grows tax-free and comes out tax-free, and the room comes back next year. RRSP: contributions are tax-deductible now and grow tax-deferred, but withdrawals are taxed, so it pays off most when your income now is higher than in retirement. Action: Keep this ready for you to forward to Sam.

The indoor winter market at Jimmie Simpson Rec Centre runs Sundays 10:00 to 14:00 until Apr 26 2026. I don't have the start date for the outdoor season, so I'll check the market's own listing instead of guessing. Action: Look up this year's opening day and location, then add it to your calendar.

I'll read Sam's text first in case he's already planning dinner. If not, I'd skip the hotplate tonight and go with something that needs no real cooking, like a pickup or delivery order or a microwave-only meal. Action: Open Sam's message, tell you what he said, and suggest one dinner option that works around his plan.

Grace and Daniel are in Alta Vista, Ottawa, so I'll look up observations for there rather than guess at temperatures. I'll pull the weather history for Sunday the 25th covering temperature, snowfall, wind and wind chill. Action: Look up Ottawa's observed weather for last Sunday the 25th and tell you whether it was as brutal as Grace says.

Wednesday morning works: a chocolate yogurt loaf with sprinkles is one bowl, no mixer, and Leo can measure, stir and add the sprinkles. It tastes better after a few hours, so it suits an evening dessert. Since you usually have spin at 6:00 am on Wednesdays, I'd plan the baking for after you're back. Action: Send you the recipe and add the ingredients to a grocery order, noting the grocery stores open at 7:00 on Wed 31 Dec.

Cost per payment on $100 and $1000: Starter $3.20 and $29.30, Growth $2.85 and $26.25, Scale $2.40 and $22.20, and Enterprise is custom so there's no figure. I'll post the retro reminder now. Action: Post the retro reminder in #payouts-launch, and put the pricing table in a doc for you.

I'll text Nate rather than call, since he prefers texts: 'Hi Nate, are the cabinets still arriving Monday?' I already know progress invoice #NR-2207 for $6,500 was due Fri 3 Oct 2025, and I'll look for the rest in your email. Action: Send the text to Nate, then pull all Northline Renovations invoices into the reno sheet and tell you if the list looks incomplete.
Added 'get passport photos for Leo' to your to-do list. Action: Add it with no due date.

Good that the overnight check looks fine. I don't have the bakery or the cake in front of me, so I'll search past orders and emails to find which one it was. Once I find it I'd order the same cake for pickup before NYE for Sam's parents' visit. Action: Search email receipts and chats for the bakery and cake, then confirm the order details with you before placing it.

On the budget: $48,000 including a 10% contingency works out to about $43,636 base and about $4,364 of contingency. I'll compare Nate's revised quote line by line against your numbers to see how much of the contingency it already uses. Action: Pull Nate's revised quote from your email, put it next to the budget sheet, and report the gap and how much contingency is left after your review.

I'll find the all-hands email from this afternoon and pull the four things that actually affect you. Action: Read the all-hands email and send you four bullets, with any deadlines or required actions first.

I don't have the passport expiry dates in front of me, so I'll look them up instead of assuming Leo's is the one. For the Lisbon trip leaving Fri 18 Dec and back Wed 30 Dec, the usual rule is that each passport should be valid for at least three months after you leave, so anything expiring before 30 March 2027 would be a problem. Action: Find the three passports' expiry dates in your documents or notes and flag any that are too close, with renewal timing if needed.
Enjoy it, porch coffee on the first properly sunny day sounds right. The Marcus question will keep. Action: Park it for later and nudge you when your career day prep block starts.

I don't have yesterday's route or its time estimate in front of me, so I won't guess a figure. I'll look for it in our chat history and notes and compare it with how long the drive actually took. Action: Find the route and estimated drive time, then tell you what was expected without traffic compared with what you experienced.

I need Sam's parents' address and what time Leo's school pickup is on Friday, because I don't have either in front of me. I won't message Sam's parents for you, so I'll just give you the arrival estimate. Action: Check your contacts for the address and your calendar for Friday pickup time, then estimate the drive with Friday traffic and tell you the likely arrival time.

Sending the text to Hannah now. For Olivia's blurb I'll pull what's in v1 from the PRD and Linear rather than guess, and keep EFT and wire distinct if they come up. The held draft to Olivia about the GA date stays unsent. Action: Send the Hannah text, then draft the 4 to 5 line v1 blurb for the sales deck for your approval.

I'll rename the Scan_*.pdf files by scan date, using each file's creation date, and show you the plan first. If two scans share a date, I'll add a number so nothing gets overwritten. Action: List the proposed new names for the Scan_*.pdf files in Downloads, then rename them once you OK the list.

The order is on hold. From my notes, the basement kitchen has a microwave, an induction hotplate and the old fridge, and the hotplate needs flat-bottom induction pans: the cast iron works but the old aluminium pot doesn't. So this week I'd plan microwave meals and one-pan hotplate dishes in the cast iron, plus the odd takeout night. Action: Hold the order and put together a simple week of dinners that work with those three appliances.

On it: I'll build the cart with milk, eggs, bread, rice, pasta, bananas, apples, yogurt tubes, cheddar, dish soap, paper towels and the frozen veggie dumplings Sam likes, checking past orders for the right brands. The Sandbanks permit stays paused until you've asked Sam about PEC, and weekend permits usually sell out by Thursday evening, so tonight is the time to ask. Action: Build the grocery order for your confirmation before checkout, and remind you tonight to ask Sam about PEC.

Reminder it is: I'll set a payment reminder ahead of each hydro due date. For the sync, I'll find a morning next week when Aisha and Diego are both free and book 25 minutes. Action: Check all three calendars, book the first shared morning slot, and put the agenda (empty-state copy, loading skeleton, who owns the Looker link) in the invite.

I'll try Dr. Lin at Queen East Dental for Apr 22, late morning. If that day has no late-morning slot, I'll check the nearest alternatives and bring them to you before booking anything else. Action: Check Apr 22 availability, check your calendar for conflicts, and book a late-morning cleaning if there is one.

Honest answer: I can't grade it yet, because I have no lesson notes, test results or recordings of you speaking to judge from. Calendar rule saved: no meetings booked for you before 9:30 or after 17:00. Action: Add the 9:30 to 17:00 limit to your calendar rules, and get Carlos's latest feedback from you so I can give an honest read.

Friday at last, and it sounds like it earned the lol. Heads up that the meetup page needs your talk title, bio and headshot by 18 Sep, so I'll check whether anything is still outstanding. Action: Check which of the title, bio and headshot have been sent to Farah and tell you if anything is still open.

Here's a draft: 'Hi neighbours, we're having a street yard sale on Saturday Oct 4 from 9 to 1, with the 5th as the rain date. Please set up tables on your own driveway, and no early birds before 9. Hope to see you out there.' Action: Post it to the street group chat once you say go, or adjust the tone first.

Welcome back, glad the drive was fine. A Tuesday after a trip always feels like Thursday. Action: Check your calendar and inbox for anything that needs you today and send you a short list so you can decide what can wait.

Congratulations on the half marathon: 2:04:37 at the Toronto Waterfront 21K, with Marcus pulling you through, is a big first. I'll remind you Fridays at 15:00 to post the payouts status update in #payouts-launch by 16:00, and pre-draft the five red/amber/green bullets from Linear. Friday evenings stay clear for pizza and movie night. Action: Create the recurring Friday 15:00 reminder, block Friday evenings (tell me the hours if you want a specific window), and save the race result (2025-10-19, 2:04:37) to your running record.

Riverside Drain & Plumbing (4.7, Broadview Ave) is the 24/7 emergency option and the one you'd planned to call, so I'd try them first for today or Monday. East End Plumbing Co. (4.8, Queen St E) has Tue 21 Oct 8-10 and Wed 22 Oct 13-15 openings, so it can't do today or Monday. A frost-free replacement beats a washer fix, so I'll ask about that. Action: Contact Riverside about today or Monday, and fall back to East End's Tuesday slot if they can't come.

Aisha prefers async Slack threads and wants specs at least two weeks before sprint planning, so I'd send her a short message instead of setting up a meeting. It would propose cutting payout nicknames and the scheduled-payouts calendar view from the Mon 25th sprint and ask her to confirm by Thursday. Action: Draft that Slack message to Aisha for your approval and set a Thursday morning reminder to follow up if she hasn't replied.

Here's a note to your mom: 'Hi Mummy, from this week our call is on Saturdays at 8:30 am my time, which is 6:00 pm for you. Sunday mornings are taken by Leo's soccer now. Hope Kabir and Ira can join.' Kabir gets the same new time. Action: Send the note to your mom, change the recurring event to Saturdays 8:30 am Toronto time, tell Kabir, and check whether the Mumbai time shifts when Toronto changes its clocks.

I'll book Ascari Enoteca for Sat 16 Aug at 19:00 for five: it's quieter than the other option and has a kids' butter pasta for Leo. For Vancouver, I'll look at flights for the three of you leaving Oct 10 and returning Oct 13. Action: Book the Ascari table, then search Oct 10 to 13 fares from home to Vancouver for three and send you the best options.
Night, and congratulations again on shipping Instant Payouts. Action: None.

Here's a draft: 'Hi, thanks for organizing the street party. I can take the 2-4pm volunteer slot at the lemonade table, but I won't be able to help with setup. Looking forward to it. Riya' Action: Save it as a draft for your review before sending.

Per my notes as of 26 Aug, PAY-1182 (GA readiness checklist, still needs Legal and Support sign-off owners) and PAY-1190 (GA announcement email copy, your call) are the ones blocking the GA milestone, and PAY-1216 (support macro) needs your tone review. That may be out of date, so I'll check live in Linear before you plan for standup. Action: Pull the currently blocked PAY tickets from Linear, update this list, and put the quickest to clear first.
